messages:
kai: Quick sync — customers report misroutes when X-Client-Context contradicts User-Agent. We're currently using UA as last resort. Thoughts on changing precedence to: 1) Signed assertion header (X-Redwood-Assert), 2) X-Client-Context, 3) UA?
jess: agree on signed first. UA is noisy and spoofable. :thumbsup:
maria: are there any customers relying on current UA fallback? we need telemetry before flipping.
sam: we have ~120k requests/day that hit UA-fallback path per last 24h. I can add a metric flagging when UA used for routing.
kai: perfect — let's emit tag `routing.path=ua-fallback` and `routing.evidence=[signed,clientctx,ua]` for debugging. Also add `quota.charge_source=original-header` so billing audit is clear.
jess: low-level concern: signed assertions require KMS verification which adds ~3ms. ok for canary but documentable.
maria: for rollout UX, console toggle to "prefer signed assertions" + rollout percentage. ops can enable per-tenant.
oliver: +1. Add an automated alert if UA-fallback rate spikes >2% of traffic for a tenant.
sam: I'll open an infra PR to add telemetry + alerting. snippet for routing rule I propose:
```
match: any
route:
  - if: header['X-Redwood-Assert'] && verify_signed(header['X-Redwood-Assert'])
    target: tenant-shard-signed
  - if: header['X-Client-Context']
    target: tenant-shard-clientctx
  - else:
    target: tenant-shard-ua-fallback
```
kai: annotate that UA-fallback should be rate-limited and opt-in for Dedicated pools; otherwise risk spoofing eviction.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: staging/routing-v2 at 03:00 UTC.
jess: also add note in docs about spoof risk and recommend SDKs to set `X-Redwood-Assert` for server-side calls.
maria: timeline? can we do telemetry + console toggle this sprint?
sam: telemetry PR by EOD, console toggle + canary next week.
kai: thanks. action items: sam->telemetry PR, sam->routing PR, jess->docs blurb, maria->console toggle spec. We'll reconvene after staging deploy. :rocket:
